name: server
//version: Deliberately left at 0.0.0 and never bumped: this package is private and never published, and the running version of the product is declared once, by the repository root package.json. One place to bump means two version strings in this repository can never disagree about which build is running.
author: Christian Mariani

scripts.//test: Ends on a sweep, not just starts with one: the daemon-backed passes leave the run's shared registry container up on purpose, so that every file after the first reuses it instead of restarting one. Nothing else is meant to outlive the pass, so the last thing a whole pass does is put the machine back as it found it.
scripts.test: npm run test:typecheck && npm run test:unit && npm run test:api && npm run test:exclusive && npm run test:sweep
scripts.//test:registry: The one step allowed to talk to a registry on the internet, and the reason no test has to: it brings up the run's own registry:2 on this machine and seeds it with every image the tests pull. Idempotent end to end, so an already-prepared registry is the normal case and one file run directly gets the same arrangement. The e2e suite runs this exact command from its global setup.
scripts.//test:api: One file at a time (--test-concurrency=1), like the exclusive pass and the e2e suite: every file drives the same daemon, so files in parallel turn contention into failures that say nothing about the product, and a file that stalls stalls behind a wall of unrelated output.
scripts.test:api: npm run test:sweep && npm run test:images && npm run test:registry && VEXEL_DATA_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vexel-server-test-data" node --experimental-test-module-mocks --import tsx --test-reporter=dot --test-concurrency=1 --test "test/api/**/*.test.ts"
scripts.test:exclusive: npm run test:sweep && npm run test:images && npm run test:registry && VEXEL_DATA_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vexel-server-test-data" node --experimental-test-module-mocks --import tsx --test-reporter=dot --test-concurrency=1 --test "test/exclusive/**/*.test.ts"
